data.body:
ALL ELEVEN ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA VERIFIED IN-SESSION BY PROBE. Evidence per criterion:

1. ROOT CAUSE A (uv shadowing) — PROVEN BOTH WAYS.
     original PATH order -> /Users/joeoakhart/.local/bin/uv   uv 0.7.18 (2025-07-01)
     fixed PATH order    -> /opt/homebrew/bin/uv              uv 0.12.0 (Homebrew 2026-07-28)
   pipx >=1.8 requires uv>=0.9.17, so the original order could never satisfy it.

2. ROOT CAUSE B (venv pinned to the pip backend) — PROVEN AND NOT OVERRIDABLE.
   pipx_metadata.json read `backend = pip` before and reads `backend = uv` after. Critically,
   `pipx install --force --backend uv` against the OLD venv was IGNORED: identical
   `error: resolution-too-deep`, metadata still `pip`. Only uninstall+reinstall changed it.

3. THE UPDATER COMPLETES — exit 0, and last-good.sha advanced off 4dd9172b9 (Jul 17) to
   25fa6107f (tip of main).

4. IT WORKS UNDER LAUNCHD, NOT JUST BY HAND — `launchctl kickstart -k` then
   `launchctl print` reports `last exit code = 0`, where it read 1 before. This was the criterion
   that mattered: every by-hand run inherits a rich shell environment, and launchd supplies a
   minimal one, so the by-hand passes proved nothing about the scheduled job.

5. THE INSTALL PATH IS EXERCISED UNDER LAUNCHD, not just the no-op branch — last-good.sha was
   temporarily rewound to 4dd9172b9 and the agent was kickstarted: it performed a REAL install and
   advanced last-good back to 25fa6107f with `last exit code = 0`. Log:
   `2026-08-01T06:36:51Z updated -> 25fa6107f...`.

6. IDEMPOTENCE — the immediately following run logged
   `no change (already on 25fa6107f...)` and exited 0. No needless reinstall.

7. THE MUTATION BITES — restoring the original PATH order reproduces the exact failure verbatim:
   `pipx needs uv>=0.9.17, but /Users/joeoakhart/.local/bin/uv reports 0.7.18`. The one-line fix is
   load-bearing, not incidental.

8. THE REPORTED SYMPTOM IS GONE — the GLOBAL build parses the dict-shaped `activate`:
   `registry.effective_criteria('.')` returns 44 criteria where it previously raised CriteriaError.

9. THE GATE ACTUALLY RUNS ON THE GLOBAL BUILD — a real `rebar review-plan d8ef --ref HEAD` invoked
   with the GLOBAL build reported `llm_ran: True`, `llm_unavailable: None`, `llm_error: None`,
   runner pydantic_ai, model claude-sonnet-4-6. Compare the reported failure signature:
   `llm_ran: false` + `llm_unavailable: true` + the CriteriaError. This is the end-to-end proof, and
   it is stronger than criterion 8 alone because it exercises the whole gate rather than the parse.

10. THE SMOKE-TEST/ROLLBACK GUARD IS INTACT — the script's two smoke commands both exit 0 against
    the freshly installed build: `rebar --help` -> 0, `rebar list --help` -> 0. So the gate that
    protects last-good.sha still functions; a bad build would still roll back.

11. THE KNOWLEDGE IS RECORDED — docs/local-env-main-tracking.local.md now documents, in its Caveats,
    that PATH order is load-bearing; that uv is a HARD requirement so `--backend pip` is not a valid
    workaround for this package (it dies on resolution-too-deep with nine extras); that an existing
    pipx venv PINS its backend and `--backend uv` will not override it; and that update.log — not the
    0-byte launchd logs — is the diagnostic file.

SCOPE OF THE FIX: one line of ~/.local/bin/rebar-dev-update.sh (PATH precedence) plus its
explanatory comment, and recreating the pipx venv. The `pipx install` line is UNTOUCHED. No
repository code changed, no dependency added, no test weakened.

WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT IN THIS TICKET: the durable hardening — making a stale installed build fail
LOUDLY instead of as a plain INDETERMINATE — is split to bug af77 (linked discovered_from this
ticket). That is a repo change with its own review; it must not hold an environment repair open. This
close asserts the ENVIRONMENT is fixed and verified, not that the reporting defect that hid it for two
weeks is fixed.

RESIDUAL HAZARD, recorded not fixed: ~/.local/bin/uv 0.7.18 still shadows uv for any process whose
PATH prefers ~/.local/bin — including an interactive shell (`which -a uv` lists it first). I did not
delete a 35 MB binary of unclear ownership; `uv self update` refuses it because the standalone
installer manages ~/.langflow/uv. Worth an operator cleanup decision.
